beef-with-vegetables-including-carrots-b.title: Beef with Vegetables (Carrots, Broccoli, Dark‑Green Leafy Greens)

content.title: About
content.content: Beef cooked together with carrots, broccoli and dark‑green leafy vegetables is a balanced dish that provides high‑quality protein, vitamins and minerals. The recipe excludes potatoes and tomato‑based sauce, making it suitable for diets that limit starches and acidic sauces.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beef is one of the richest sources of heme iron, essential for oxygen transport in the blood.
Broccoli contains sulforaphane, a compound studied for its potential anti‑cancer properties.
Carrots are high in beta‑carotene, which the body converts into vitamin A.
Dark‑green leafy greens (spinach, kale, collard greens) are packed with vitamin K, important for blood clotting.
The combination of protein and fiber in this dish promotes long‑lasting satiety.

items.title: Supports Muscle Mass
items.content: Beef provides all essential amino acids needed for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Boosts Immune Function
items.content: Vitamin C in broccoli and beta‑carotene in carrots enhance the body’s defense mechanisms.

items.title: Bone Health
items.content: Calcium and vitamin K from leafy greens contribute to bone mineralization.

items.title: Vision Support
items.content: Beta‑carotene and lutein from carrots and broccoli help maintain sharp eyesight.

items.title: Blood Sugar Regulation
items.content: Fiber from the vegetables slows glucose absorption, beneficial for pre‑diabetic individuals.

items.title: Excess Red Meat Consumption
items.content: Eating large amounts of beef may be linked to higher cardiovascular risk if not consumed in moderation.

items.title: Beef Allergy
items.content: Some people may experience allergic reactions to beef proteins.

items.title: Sodium Content
items.content: If the dish is seasoned with salt or soy sauce, monitor total sodium intake, especially for hypertension.

items.title: Foodborne Illness
items.content: Undercooked beef can harbor pathogenic bacteria; ensure internal temperature reaches at least 63 °C (145 °F).

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot as a main course, add it to salads, wrap it in lettuce leaves for a low‑carb lunch, or pair with whole‑grain sides. A drizzle of olive oil or lemon juice can enhance flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked beef with vegetables in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 2 months. Reheat thoroughly before consuming.

blue-or-roquefort-cheese-dressing-fat-fr.title: Blue or Roquefort Cheese Dressing, Fat Free

content.title: About
content.content: Blue or Roquefort Cheese Dressing, fat free, is a creamy sauce blend based on blue or Roquefort cheese that contains no added fats. It delivers the characteristic sharp aroma of blue cheese, a smooth texture, and low calories, making it suitable for diet‑friendly meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Blue and Roquefort cheeses are produced with Penicillium roqueforti cultures that give them their distinctive flavor and blue‑marbled appearance.
The fat‑free version retains flavor by using skimmed milk proteins and natural cheese extracts.
Its combination of creamy taste and tanginess makes it popular in salads, vegetable dishes, and as a dip for seafood.
In the United States the sauce is often served with chicken wings and steak.
Sodium levels in the fat‑free version are usually lower than in traditional cheese dressings.

items.title: Low Calorie
items.content: The absence of added fats reduces the energy content, which can help with weight management.

items.title: Probiotic Content
items.content: Cheese cultures used in production may support a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Source of Calcium
items.content: Cheese ingredients retain some calcium, important for bones and teeth.

items.title: Vitamin B12
items.content: Provides vitamin B12, which supports nerve function and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Low Saturated Fat
items.content: No added fats means lower saturated fat intake, beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Milk Allergy
items.content: Contains dairy proteins and may trigger reactions in individuals allergic to milk.

items.title: High Sodium Content
items.content: Some formulations contain notable salt levels; people with hypertension should monitor portions.

items.title: Mold Sensitivity
items.content: Those sensitive to mold spores may experience discomfort.

items.title: Not Vegan
items.content: Based on dairy ingredients, it is unsuitable for vegans.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Add the dressing to salads, use as a dip for vegetable sticks, drizzle over roasted vegetables, chicken or fish, or blend with cottage cheese for an extra‑creamy spread.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 2‑4 °C in a sealed container. Once opened, consume within 7‑10 days. Discard if the smell or taste changes.

cauliflower-frozen-cooked-with-butter-or.title: Cauliflower, frozen, cooked with butter or margarine

content.title: About
content.content: Frozen cauliflower cooked with butter or margarine is a ready‑to‑eat vegetable product that is blanched, flash‑frozen and then sautéed or stewed in fat. It retains most of its nutrients, has a mild buttery flavor and a tender texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cauliflower belongs to the cruciferous family, along with broccoli and Brussels sprouts.
Freezing after blanching preserves the bright white color and crisp structure.
Cooking with butter or margarine enhances absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins A and K.
Frozen vegetables are widely used in restaurants for quick meal preparation.
Cauliflower is rich in glucosinolates, compounds that may have anti‑cancer properties.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Good source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: One cup provides about 70 kcal, making it suitable for weight‑controlled diets.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Phytonutrients help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Cruciferous allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience an allergic reaction to cauliflower.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some versions are salted; those monitoring sodium should check the label.

items.title: Added fats
items.content: Using a lot of butter or margarine increases the product’s calorie density.

items.title: Thyroid considerations
items.content: Cauliflower contains goitrogens, which in excess may affect thyroid function.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the product in a skillet or microwave, season to taste. It works well as a side dish, in soups, stews, pasta, or mixed vegetable medleys.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen cauliflower in a freezer at –18 °C. After thawing, use within 2–3 days and store in an airtight container in the refrigerator.

content.title: About
content.content: XS Gold Plus is an energy drink containing caffeine, taurine, B‑vitamins and guarana extracts. It is designed to boost alertness, improve focus and accelerate metabolism. The drink has a bright gold color and a distinctive fruity‑citrus taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: XS Gold Plus was developed in Russia and has been produced since 2018.
It contains 200 mg of caffeine, equivalent to two espresso shots.
The formula includes electrolytes (sodium, potassium) to support fluid balance during exercise.
Packaging is a 250 ml aluminum can, fully recyclable.
The line offers several flavors, such as Tropical, Berry and Coffee.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Caffeine and taurine stimulate the central nervous system, increasing vigor and reducing perceived fatigue.

items.title: Improved concentration
items.content: B‑vitamins (B3, B5, B6, B12) support neurotransmitter synthesis, helping mental focus and reaction speed.

items.title: Metabolism support
items.content: Guarana provides natural caffeine that speeds up metabolic rate and aids calorie burning.

items.title: Electrolyte balance
items.content: Sodium and potassium help prevent dehydration during intense physical activity.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Vitamin C and plant extracts have antioxidant properties that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Excess caffeine intake
items.content: High caffeine doses may cause anxiety, insomnia, rapid heartbeat and increased blood pressure.

items.title: Not for children and pregnant women
items.content: Due to its high caffeine content, the product is not recommended for persons under 18, pregnant or nursing women.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Caffeine can amplify the effects of certain stimulants and reduce the efficacy of sedatives.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: The drink may contain trace amounts of gluten, soy or dairy, which should be considered by allergic individuals.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Acidic flavorings may irritate the stomach lining if consumed frequently.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Consume one 250 ml can 30‑60 minutes before physical activity or when energy drops. Do not exceed 2–3 servings per day. Drink chilled and store in a cool place, away from direct sunlight.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cans in a dry, cool place protected from direct sunlight. Once opened, finish within 24 hours. Do not store at temperatures above 30 °C.

content.title: About
content.content: Steamed cod is a delicate white-fleshed marine fish, rich in high‑quality protein and low in fat. Steaming preserves its natural flavor, moisture, and most nutrients, making it a light and healthy dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cod is one of the most widely harvested fish in the North Atlantic and Pacific oceans.
The flesh contains few calories (about 80 kcal per 100 g) but is abundant in B‑vitamins and minerals.
Cod can grow quickly, reaching up to 1 m in length and 20 kg in weight.
Steamed cod is a traditional dish in Scandinavian cuisine, often served with herbs and lemon.
Steaming retains up to 90 % of the omega‑3 fatty acids present in the fish.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Cod protein is highly digestible and supports tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The low amount of saturated fat makes it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Omega‑3s promote heart health and reduce inflammatory processes.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B12, B6, and niacin help maintain nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Contains selenium, iodine, and phosphorus, important for thyroid health and bones.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to marine fish.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Cod can accumulate mercury and other toxins; choose fish from reputable sources.

items.title: Improper storage
items.content: Incorrect refrigeration can lead to bacterial growth and spoilage.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Steamed cod can be served with lemon, fresh herbs, a drizzle of olive oil, or a light yogurt‑based sauce. It pairs well with boiled potatoes, quinoa, vegetable sides, or can be added to salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh cod in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C, wrapped in plastic film, for no more than 2 days. Frozen cod can be stored at –18 °C for up to 3 months. Before cooking, check for any ammonia‑like odor.

content.title: About
content.content: Salmon is a marine fish of the Salmonidae family, known for its delicate flavor and high nutritional value. When baked or broiled, salmon retains most of its beneficial nutrients while developing a fragrant crust and juicy flesh.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Salmon can migrate from the ocean to rivers to spawn, traveling distances of over 3,000 km.
Wild salmon contains more omega‑3 fatty acids than farm‑raised salmon.
The pink‑red color of the flesh comes from astaxanthin, a powerful antioxidant pigment.
Salmon is one of the few fish species that live both in saltwater and freshwater during their life cycle.
In Japan, salmon is often grilled (yaki‑sake), while in Scandinavian countries it is commonly baked with herbs.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Salmon provides EPA and DHA, which support heart health, reduce inflammation, and promote brain function.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: A 100 g serving delivers about 20 g of complete protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of vitamin D
items.content: Salmon is one of the few food sources of vitamin D, important for bone health and immunity.

items.title: Contains selenium
items.content: Selenium in salmon supports antioxidant defenses and thyroid function.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: B12, B6, and niacin in salmon help maintain energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Contaminant risk
items.content: Some salmon may contain mercury, PCBs, and other toxins; choosing wild‑caught or reputable farmed sources reduces this risk.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Individuals with fish allergies may experience reactions ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Digestive discomfort with large portions
items.content: Very fatty portions can cause stomach upset in people with sensitive digestion.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Salmon can be baked in the oven with lemon, herbs, and olive oil, grilled or pan‑seared until golden. It is also used in salads, sushi, pastas, and as a fillet steak.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Fresh salmon should be kept in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C and used within 2 days, tightly wrapped in plastic. Frozen salmon can be stored up to 6 months at –18 °C. Before cooking, check for a fresh, mild scent; a strong “fishy” odor indicates spoilage.

content.title: About
content.content: Melon (Cucumis melo) is a sweet, juicy fruit that grows on a trailing vine, with varieties such as cantaloupe, honeydew, and galia. It has a rind that can be netted or smooth and flesh that ranges from pale green to orange. Melons have a fragrant aroma and a sweet taste and are eaten fresh in slices and cubes, in salads, and in drinks.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Melons are related to cucumbers, watermelons, and squash.
Cantaloupe has orange flesh and a netted rind, while honeydew has pale green flesh and a smooth rind.
A ripe melon often has a sweet, fragrant smell at the stem end.
Melons are about 90 percent water.
Melons have been cultivated for thousands of years in Africa and Asia.

items.title: Hydrating
items.content: Melons are mostly water, making them refreshing.

items.title: Provides vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and skin.

items.title: Provides vitamin A
items.content: Orange-fleshed melons such as cantaloupe contain carotenoids that the body can convert into vitamin A.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium supports normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Melon is low in calories for its volume.

items.title: Food safety
items.content: Bacteria such as Salmonella and Listeria can be present on melon rinds. Wash the rind before cutting and refrigerate cut melon.

items.title: Natural sugar content
items.content: Melons contain natural sugars, so portions matter for people monitoring blood sugar.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Some people, especially those with pollen allergies, may experience itching or tingling in the mouth.

items.title: Potassium considerations
items.content: People with kidney problems or on certain medications should consult a healthcare professional about potassium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Melon can be sliced or cubed and eaten fresh, added to fruit salads, wrapped in thin slices of cured ham, blended into juices and smoothies, or frozen into sorbets. Chill it before serving. Remove the seeds and rind before eating.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep uncut melons at room temperature until ripe, then refrigerate them. Wash the rind before cutting. Store cut melon in an airtight container in the refrigerator and eat it within three days. Discard melon that smells fermented or is slimy.

multiple-meat-sandwich-on-white-with-che.title: Multiple meat sandwich on white bread with cheese

content.title: About
content.content: The multiple meat sandwich on white bread with cheese (1856) combines soft white bun, melted cheese and a mix of meat fillings: ham, chicken breast, beef and salami. The product is ready‑to‑eat, individually wrapped and should be stored at 0 °C to +4 °C.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Multi‑meat sandwiches are popular in cafeterias and fast‑service restaurants for quick serving.
Combining different meats enhances flavor complexity and provides a broader amino‑acid profile.
White bread gives a mild backdrop that lets the cheese flavor shine.
Often included in “quick lunch” packs in supermarkets.
Sodium content is usually higher than average because of the cured meats.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Meat fillings supply high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Cheese contributes calcium, supporting bone health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and cheese provide B1, B2, B6 and B12 vitamins important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: The sandwich offers a quick calorie boost, convenient for busy schedules.

items.title: Dietary fiber from bread
items.content: Although white bread is low in fiber, it still adds a small amount of dietary fiber.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: Salt used in the meats and cheese can contribute to elevated blood pressure.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: People with lactose intolerance or cheese allergy should avoid this product.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Processed meat often contains nitrites and other additives that should be limited.

items.title: Storage requirements
items.content: If the cold chain is broken, the sandwich can spoil quickly and cause foodborne illness.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich is ready to eat straight from the pack. For a softer cheese texture, heat briefly in a microwave (30‑40 seconds). Adding fresh vegetables such as tomato, cucumber or lettuce can increase nutritional value.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 0 °C to +4 °C. Shelf life is printed on the package, typically 7‑10 days from production date. Discard if an off‑odor or discoloration appears.

content.title: About
content.content: Oatmeal consists of whole oat grains that have been processed for easy preparation. The reduced‑sugar version contains less added sweeteners while retaining the characteristic nutty flavor and nutritional benefits.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Oats are one of the oldest cultivated crops, grown for over 5,000 years.
Oat flakes can be steel‑cut or instant; both work well in low‑sugar diets.
Beta‑glucan, a soluble fiber in oats, helps regulate blood glucose levels.
Oats are a staple in vegan cooking because of their natural protein and iron content.
Reduced‑sugar oatmeal achieves lower sweetness by cutting added syrups and using alternative sweeteners.

items.title: Rich in beta‑glucan
items.content: Beta‑glucan helps lower cholesterol and improves insulin sensitivity.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Complex carbohydrates provide sustained energy and prolonged satiety.

items.title: Contains plant protein
items.content: Oats provide about 13 % protein, beneficial for vegetarians and athletes.

items.title: High in B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B5, and folate support metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Provides minerals
items.content: Magnesium, iron, and zinc in oats aid muscle function and immune support.

items.title: Oat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to oats or the gluten‑like proteins they contain.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce mineral absorption; soaking or fermenting oats can mitigate this.

items.title: Added sweeteners
items.content: Certain reduced‑sugar products use artificial sweeteners, which may cause discomfort for sensitive people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Prepare oatmeal with water or milk, then add fruit, nuts, seeds, and spices. For a quick breakfast, pour hot liquid over the flakes and let sit for 2–3 minutes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the package in a cool, dry place, tightly sealed. After opening, transfer to an airtight container and use within 3–4 weeks.

content.title: About
content.content: Sweet potato fries, frozen are sliced batata strips that are blanched and flash‑frozen to preserve flavor, color, and nutrients. They are perfect for quick preparation in an oven or deep‑fryer.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sweet potatoes are richer in beta‑carotene than regular potatoes, giving them a bright orange hue.
Freezing immediately after blanching locks in a crisp texture after cooking.
Sweet potatoes originate from tropical and subtropical regions but can be cultivated in cooler climates as well.
Compared with regular potatoes, sweet potatoes contain less starch and more dietary fiber.
Frozen products undergo strict quality controls to ensure safety and uniform portion sizes.

items.title: Rich in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene converts to vitamin A in the body, supporting vision and immune function.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C helps protect cells from oxidative stress and enhances iron absorption.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Lower glycemic index
items.content: Sweet potatoes have a lower glycemic index than regular potatoes, helping maintain steadier blood sugar levels.

items.title: Provides potassium
items.content: Potassium supports fluid balance and normal heart function.

items.title: Sweet potato allergy
items.content: Rare, but some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to sweet potatoes.

items.title: Sodium content in prepared dishes
items.content: Adding salt or sauces can raise the sodium level of the final dish.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: While nutritious, frying or baking with excess oil increases the calorie count.

items.title: Choking hazard for children
items.content: Small pieces can pose a choking risk for young children.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bake at 200 °C for 12‑15 minutes or deep‑fry until golden. Serve as a side, in burgers, with dips, or as a healthy snack. Sprinkle with spices such as paprika, garlic, or rosemary for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen product in a freezer at –18 °C or lower. After thawing, cook immediately and do not store at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
